key_insight: A mixed unfitted finite element method computes photonic-crystal band structures on geometry-independent meshes while preserving a shifted de Rham structure that rules out spurious modes.
engineering_relevance: The approach avoids interface-fitted meshing and remeshing when inclusion geometries change, supporting efficient photonic-crystal design studies.
method: Apply the Floquet–Bloch transform to periodic Maxwell eigenvalue problems.
Use a uniform background mesh and impose periodicity by directly identifying degrees of freedom.
Construct compatible mixed finite element pairs with cut-position-independent inf-sup stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports optimal eigenvalue and eigenspace convergence with mesh-size- and interface-position-independent constants, supported by extensive 2D and 3D numerical experiments.
watch_item: Geometry-independent meshing still requires careful treatment of cut elements and preservation of the compatible mixed discretization.
paper_title: Mixed Unfitted finite element approximation of band structures in photonic crystals
